headline: Personal Income and Outlays, January 2025
summary: January consumer spending declined 0.2% in nominal terms while the PCE price index rose 0.3% over the month. This release gave investors both a spending signal and an inflation update.

headline: How major US stock indexes fared Tuesday, 2/25/2025
summary: Shares weakened as concerns about tariffs and inflation weighed on consumers. Treasury yields also fell as demand for safer assets increased.

headline: Wall Street falls sharply as Nvidia tumbles 8.5% and AI mania falters
summary: Nvidia fell 8.5% after its results as enthusiasm for artificial-intelligence shares weakened. The 10-year Treasury yield edged higher that day, showing that daily bond moves differed within the broader window.

headline: Producer Price Indexes — January 2026
summary: US producer prices rose 0.5% in January and 2.9% over the preceding year. The release showed that price pressure remained relevant when investors assessed the interest-rate outlook.

headline: Dow drops 400 after trimming an early plunge of 1,200 as oil prices climb even higher
summary: The widening war with Iran pushed oil prices higher and shares lower. Treasury yields rose amid inflation concerns, illustrating pressure on stocks and bonds at the same time.

headline: Adjusting Imports of Automobiles and Automobile Parts into the United States
summary: The administration announced a 25% tariff on imported cars and certain parts. The car tariff was scheduled to begin on 3 April; businesses with international supply chains faced a change in future import costs.

headline: Gross Domestic Product, Fourth Quarter 2024 — Third Estimate
summary: The published estimate put fourth-quarter real GDP growth at a 2.4% annual rate, slower than the third quarter. It described a still-expanding economy before the coming trade-policy changes.

headline: Personal Income and Outlays, February 2025
summary: February PCE prices rose 0.3% over the month; excluding food and energy, prices rose 0.4% and were 2.8% above a year earlier. Investors had to weigh continuing inflation pressure alongside growth and trade-policy risks.
